name: aggregate_coverage_gating
why_a_second_gate: config/coverage-gate.json governs the per-scope check and is recorded as PASS but NOT WIRED, because a lower-tail quantile over 8 reference periods produces roughly 43 scope flags per real period. Wiring that signal to the escalation path would trade a 100% alarm rate for a different kind of noise. That is a *different decision* from the per-scope check's accuracy, so it gets its own registration rather than an edit to the first gate. The first gate is left exactly as run.
hypothesis: Gating per-entity missing escalation on AGGREGATE coverage - did this entity type lose distinct counterpart keys relative to its own trailing history - is a decision-grade signal, because it asks the question the escalation actually means ('did we lose products / did we lose stores') rather than 'did any one of 38 scopes twitch'.

design.signal: for each configured entity key column, the number of distinct counterpart keys present in the appended period, compared against that column's own trailing per-period counts at the registered lower-tail quantile
design.threshold: per entity column, from that column's own history; never a global constant and never an absolute expected count
design.held_constant: identical real suite, identical periods, identical quantile. Only whether the aggregate gate is consulted changes.

arms.ungated: the current behaviour, which produced a 100% alarm rate across 27 real refreshes
arms.gated: LATEST_WEEK_MISSING escalates to MISSING_STORES / MISSING_PRODUCTS only when the corresponding aggregate coverage regressed

acceptance.max_fire_rate: over the real period sequence, the fraction of periods in which the aggregate gate fires. Must be at or below max_fire_rate. This is the number that decides whether the gate is usable as an escalation gate at all.
acceptance.min_injected_detection_rate: over injected aggregate drops at or above min_detectable_drop_fraction, the fraction the gate must catch, so that wiring the gate cannot silently blind the escalation path.

claims_limit: Passing authorises wiring the aggregate coverage gate into the escalation path as an opt-in configuration, and nothing more. It does not confer validated-real, does not establish a production false-positive rate, and does not resolve the residual per-entity sensitivity: with the gate on, a genuine per-entity drop that does not move aggregate coverage is still suppressed. That limitation is inherent to any scope-level gate and is recorded rather than hidden.
note: Written BEFORE the wiring was implemented or measured. If it fails it is reported as failed and not retro-fitted.
